summary.short: Committee report recommending a fifth paragraph in Article 20 Quáter of Mexico's General Law on Women's Access to a Life Free of Violence, sanctioning intentional non-consensual generation by technological means of intimate sexual images, videos or audios simulating sexual acts, and their dissemination.
summary.long: Committee report (dictamen) of the Chamber of Deputies' Gender Equality Committee, dated 21 October 2025 and published in the Gaceta of 17 February 2026, on a PAN initiative presented 29 April 2025 concerning generative artificial intelligence and gender-based digital violence. The decree adds a fifth paragraph to Article 20 Quáter of the General Law on Women's Access to a Life Free of Violence. It sanctions intentional conduct of generating, wholly or partly by technological means, intimate sexual images, videos or audios that simulate sexual acts or pornographic representations of a person, without consent, approval or authorization, and the dissemination, distribution, publication or sharing of such material even when created by those means. The decree states that such conduct 'se sancionará' and sets no penalty amount. The report's comparison table marks the commission's column as keeping current text for Article 5 and Article 20 Septies, and considers the initiative's Article 20 Septies repetitive of existing Chapter IV Ter provisions. The decree enters into force the day after publication in the Diario Oficial de la Federación. The document is a committee report and does not record plenary approval.

notes: Committee report (dictamen) with a draft decree. Inconsistency: the title and header say the decree reforms Art. 5 and adds Art. 20 Septies, but the operative text ('Único') only adds a fifth paragraph to Art. 20 Quáter. The comparison table marks Art. 5 and Art. 20 Septies as 'Se mantiene texto vigente' in the commission column, and the proposed generative-AI definition for Art. 5 XVIII is not in the operative decree. The commission reasoning (Considerations SEXTA and SÉPTIMA) finds the initiative largely repeats existing LGAMVLV provisions on digital violence. The proposed paragraph sanctions non-consensual generation or dissemination of intimate sexual images simulating sexual acts, by technological means, but this text states no penalty. Source is OCR of a scanned gazette PDF; the comparison table is garbled, so quotes come from OCR. Dates: initiative presented 29 April 2025; deadline extended to 31 August 2027; dictamen dated 21 October 2025; gazette 17 February 2026. No floor vote appears in this document; entry into force is the day after DOF publication, per the proposal's transitory article.
